title: AIRSpeed Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6XXX), DC AVN
raw_text:
4. MOS 6608, AIRSpeed Officer (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO)
NMOS (6XXX), DC AVN

    a. Summary. AIRSpeed Officers are assigned to selected headquarters and
staffs. They are trained to institute a culture of self-sustaining,
continuous process improvement aligned toward delivering increased readiness
at reduced resource cost. AIRSpeed Officers are responsible to provide the
planning, training, integration, sustainment, and monitoring of best business
practices (Theory of Constraints (TOC), LEAN, and Six Sigma within aviation
logistics.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be trained in Jonah.

            (2) Must be trained and certified as supply chain design expert
(SCDE).

            (3) Must be trained and certified as supply chain technical expert
(SCTE).

        (4) Must possess MOS 6XXX:         aviation maintenance, avionics, aviation
ordnance, or aviation supply MOS.



                                           1-253                        Enclosure (1)
 1138                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



    c. Requirements. Must complete AIRSpeed Black Belt Job Qualification
Requirement (JQR) as defined by COMNAVAIRFOR, or equivalent course as
approved by HQMC Aviation (ASL).

       d.   Duties

        (1) Coordinate, support, and monitor TOC process designs and
deployments.

        (2) Coach LEAN events, including Rapid Improvement Events (RIEs),
Value Stream Analyses (VSAs), and 5S events.

        (3) Act as team leader for complex LEAN Six Sigma (LSS) events or
projects where statistical analysis is required.

        (4) Ensure all AIRSpeed department core members are Green Belt
qualified, at a minimum.

            (5) Be responsible for administering and evaluating AIRSpeed
events.      Function as liaison with external consultants and/or organizations.

        (6) Ensure sustainment of improvement through use of follow-ups and
refresher training.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Logisticians 13-1081.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
